chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub from Abu Ayyub al-Kazzaz from Mihzam from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a slave woman under the ownership of a free man who divorced her during a period of purity without sexual intercourse, with one revocable divorce, and then she was freed after he had divorced her for thirty days, and her waiting period had not yet expired. He said: If she is freed before her waiting period expires, she observes the waiting period of a free woman from the day he divorced her, and he has the right of return (raj'ah) over her before the expiration of the waiting period. If he divorced her with two divorces, one after the other, and then she was freed before the expiration of her waiting period, then he has no right of return over her, and her waiting period is the waiting period of a slave woman.

key_terms.الرَّجْعَةُ: Right of return (to the marriage without a new contract)

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period and right of return for a slave woman who is divorced and then freed?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar clarifies the complex interplay between manumission and divorce, establishing that if a slave woman is freed before her iddah expires, she transitions to the status of a free woman for the purpose of the waiting period. It further refines the right of revocable return (raj'ah) by distinguishing between single and double divorces, ensuring the owner's rights are preserved or limited according to the specific timing of her emancipation relative to the completion of her iddah.
